network.title: Cluster Networking and Pod Readiness Probes
network.raw_content:
# Network Diagnostics Runbook

## Pod Restart vs Network Fault
A pod terminating with exit code 137 is killed by the kernel cgroup OOM killer, not by a network fault. Before suspecting the network layer, confirm the CNI is healthy:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=cilium
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- wget -qO- http://ingestion-worker:8080/healthz
```
If readiness probes only fail during the restart window and service endpoints recover between restarts, the network layer is healthy and the fault is in the workload itself.

database.raw_content:
# Database Ingestion Queue Runbook
Verify that PostgreSQL is not blocking chunk insertions:
```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM documents WHERE status = 'pending';
```

application.title: Document Ingestion Worker Memory Profiling
application.raw_content:
# Ingestion Worker Memory Leak Runbook

## Root Cause
PDF parser loads the entire document into an unbounded byte slice instead of streaming chunks via `io.Reader`. When parsing documents > 30MB with embedded images, the Go heap inflates exponentially, triggering kernel cgroups OOM killer.

## Remediation
1. Replace `io.ReadAll` with buffered streaming parser in `ExtractTextChunks`.
2. In the interim, increase Kubernetes container memory limits from 2Gi to 4Gi.

## Kubernetes Resource Limits
## Verification
Inspect pod events and resource quota saturation:
```bash
kubectl describe pod -l app=ingestion-worker
kubectl top pod -l app=ingestion-worker
```
